subject: DPIA sampling scenarios and processor log export request
messages:
From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@finbank.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: security@finbank.com
Date: Thu, 08 Jul 2027 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: Request: DPIA sampling scenarios + Art.30 ledger export

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the DPA conversation last week. As we prepare for our internal DPIA and downstream audit, the security team has two asks we hope Redwood can help with:

1) Can you provide a short set of proposed sampling scenarios (2–3 pages or a spreadsheet) you would expect a customer to use when validating DSP/processor controls for LLM inference? We want to include examples of sampling by: job/role, tenant scope, and time-window (e.g., 48-hour token traces).

2) We need an Art.30-style ledger extract (machine-readable CSV) for the period 2027-07-01 to 2027-07-06 showing processor access events, subprocessor handoff records, and KMS wrap/unwrapped events — sufficient for our compliance team to reconstitute a retention timeline. If there are privacy constraints, please advise the minimal redaction approach.

Can you confirm feasibility and an ETA? We have an external auditor (cc'ed) who will want the file by end of week if possible.

Best,
Sara
Sara Jenkins
Senior Privacy Manager — FinBank
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@finbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Jul 2027 10:02:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Request: DPIA sampling scenarios + Art.30 ledger export

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear asks. Short answer: yes, we can produce both items but need to triage scope. Quick notes:

- Sampling scenarios: we have a draft matrix that maps sampling dimensions (customer tenant id, API route, user role, retention window, sampling probability) to evidence artifacts (call traces, KV cache keys, redacted prompt/response snapshot). We can convert that into a one-sheet spreadsheet and short guidance for auditors.

- Art.30 ledger extract: we can export a CSV with event-level rows (timestamp, event_type, principal, subprocessor_id, resource_id, kms_event_tag). For privacy we typically pseudonymize end-user identifiers (sha256) but preserve consistent hashing for traceability. If FinBank requires raw user identifiers we will need a signed SOP exception and legal approval.

Timeline proposal:
- Today EOD: we will share the sampling scenarios spreadsheet draft for your review (internal owners: Marissa + Karthik).
- Tomorrow afternoon: processor log export (CSV) with pseudonymization applied.

Can you confirm the exact columns your auditor requires and whether pseudonymization is acceptable? If acceptable, we will proceed on that cadence.

Thanks — looping in Marissa and Karthik to own the artifacts.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Privacy Operations, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: DPIA sampling scenarios + Art.30 ledger export

Sara / Naomi — attaching the draft sampling matrix and a first-pass processor log export for 2027-07-01 -> 2027-07-06. Notes and caveats below.

Attachments:
- dpia-sampling-scenarios-v1.xlsx (contains three scenario templates: tenant-scoped audit, role-based spot-check, and time-window continuity)
- processor-log-export-20270706.csv (event-level; columns: ts,event_type,principal,subprocessor_id,resource_id,kms_tag,notes)
- dpa-amendment-proposed-redlines.pdf (redlines we propose if raw identifiers are requested)

Key caveats:
- The CSV pseudonymizes end-user identifiers using a salted hash; we can provide the salt under a separate legal agreement if FinBank requires re-identification for the DPIA.
- KMS wrap/unwrapped rows are included where available; some legacy subprocessor hops only surface aggregate counts (we've called these out in the notes column).
- Sampling guidance includes suggested sample sizes for 95% confidence within short windows; these are illustrative and should be adjusted to your audit tolerance.

Action items for FinBank: please confirm whether pseudonymization is acceptable and whether the included columns meet the auditor's schema. If the auditor needs raw identifiers, we need a signed DPA amendment and an approved data access SOP (I attached proposed redlines).

ETA: If pseudonymization is acceptable, we can finalize the CSV and provide an annotated extraction log by Friday 2027-07-09 17:00 CEST. If re-identification is required, timeline becomes legal-dependent (likely 7–10 business days).

Let us know and we’ll prioritize.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Privacy Program Manager — Redwood Inference

Next steps:
- Please add a one-page README to the folder describing pseudonymization, retention windows, and the exact event types included in the export.
- Deliver the finalized CSV + README by Friday EOD CEST.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Regards,
Sara
